candidates.attacker_control: The `changenote` form field (and `page`, `ok`, and the SpamFilter hash) of a POST to Edit.jsp. Edit.jsp line 73 yields the raw value (`findParam(pageContext, "changenote")`); it is then written to the page object at lines 167-170 and saved via wiki.saveText. No escaping or character filtering is applied to this parameter on the Edit path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether the value is escaped elsewhere on the write path (Comment.jsp:86 and AttachmentServlet:516-522 do escape it, and Diff providers escape page text), whether the providers sanitize attributes on read/write (they do not; AbstractFileProvider.setCustomProperties merely skips AUTHOR/CHANGENOTE/VIEWCOUNT), whether SpamFilter sanitizes the change note (it only reads it when composing the spam-check text; it does not rewrite the attribute), and whether output escaping exists in the templates (it does not: `${changenote}` is plain EL, and the 210 template uses raw scriptlet output). Mitigation could exist if a deployment replaced the templates with `<c:out>`-based output. I could not diff this snapshot against upstream (no network/patches allowed), so I cannot prove line 73 was modified rather than an upstream oversight.
candidates.impact: Stored/persistent XSS in the wiki origin: script runs in the browser of any user viewing the affected page's Info/history (or, for attachments, the attachment list), enabling session theft, actions with the victim's privileges (including administrators), and worm-like propagation on wikis with open editing.
candidates.prerequisites: An account/permission that can save a page revision (this is often anonymous on default JSPWiki policies; the snapshot does not contain WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy, so the exact default grant set could not be verified), plus a victim who opens the Info tab of the affected page (PageInfo.jsp?page=...), where the default or 210 template renders the stored change note.
candidates.root_cause: Edit.jsp takes the attacker-supplied `changenote` request parameter and stores it as the page's WikiPage.CHANGENOTE attribute without HTML-escaping it (line 73; contrast the escaped `author`/`link` values on lines 72/75, Comment.jsp line 86, and AttachmentServlet lines 516-522, which all wrap the same kind of value in TextUtil.replaceEntities). The providers persist the attribute into page metadata and the shipped templates emit it back with no output encoding (default template: `<c:set var="changenote" .../>` followed by raw `${changenote}`, and EL does not HTML-escape; the 210 template prints it with raw `<%= changenote %>`). The missing input escape can therefore be turned into a persistent script injection.
candidates.title: Stored XSS via unescaped page change note (Edit.jsp -> InfoContent templates)
candidates.trace: POST Edit.jsp (ok set, valid spam hash) -> Edit.jsp:73 reads raw changenote -> Edit.jsp:163-170 sets modifiedPage attribute WikiPage.CHANGENOTE -> wiki.saveText (WikiEngine.java:1723-1767) -> SaveWikiPageTask.execute -> PageManager.putPageText -> FileSystemProvider.putPageText/putPageProperties (FileSystemProvider.java:55-112, writes `<version>.changenote` / `changenote` property) or VersioningFileProvider.java:519-523 -> later read back by FileSystemProvider.getPageInfo/getPageProperties (FileSystemProvider.java:134-140) or VersioningFileProvider.java:618-619 -> rendered without encoding by templates/default/InfoContent.jsp:206-207 (`${changenote}`, JSP EL is not escaped) and templates/210/InfoContent.jsp:246-249/398-400 (`<%= changenote %>`).
candidates.unverified: Runtime exploitability was not tested (no build/execution permitted). The default WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy (which determines whether anonymous users can edit) is not present in the snapshot. It is unknown whether the 210 skin is deployed, but the default template contains an equivalent raw sink. Whether custom/third-party templates escape the value is unknown.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-Site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Source-only review of the JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3-RC2 snapshot. Scope reported 1,155 model-visible files; the P1 relation index parsed 1,018 files (5,432 symbols, 15,235 call sites, 10,564 edges) and is explicitly partial: 137 files are missing from the index, including all 117 .jsp files, where this candidate's input and output sinks live, so the index contributed only navigation (auth, attachment, provider, parser, preferences areas) and every relation was re-verified against source text. I inspected the attachment upload/download path, authentication/authorization (AuthenticationManager, AuthorizationManager, WikiSession/WikiRequestWrapper, UserManager, GroupManager, JDBC/XML user and group stores), XML-RPC/MetaWeblog handlers, page providers (FileSystemProvider, VersioningFileProvider, AbstractFileProvider, BasicAttachmentProvider), parser/link/diff/render paths, SpamFilter, Installer, admin beans, the JSPWikiUserPrefs handling, and the JSP/taglib views that render user-controlled values (Edit, Comment, Delete, Rename, PageInfo, InfoContent, AttachmentTab, ProfileTab, PreferencesTab, Group views). No build, tests, or scanners were executed; no runtime data was used.
limitations: The P1 source-relation index does not cover JSPs (137 files omitted, including Edit.jsp and the InfoContent templates), so the selected candidate lies largely outside the indexed relation graph; Java companions were verified by reading source.
No build, unit/integration test, or scanner run; exploitability is inferred from source only and was not runtime-confirmed.
WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy is not part of the snapshot, so the default permission set (in particular whether anonymous users may edit pages or see the rename UI) could not be verified.
The snapshot cannot be diffed against upstream (no network or patch access), so whether Edit.jsp line 73 lost a TextUtil.replaceEntities call or reflects an upstream oversight is uncertain.
Template selection is deployment-dependent (default vs 210 vs custom skins); the default template was verified to contain a raw output sink, but other skins were only spot-checked.
Search/symbol coverage is limited to model-visible files; binary or excluded artifacts were not analyzed.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS via the `renameto` request parameter: templates/default/InfoContent.jsp:42/126 and templates/210/InfoContent.jsp:44/146 read the parameter and print it inside `value="<%= parm_renameto %>"` with no escaping (creationAuthor in the same file is escaped before `<%= %>`).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible second XSS, but the form is only emitted inside `<wiki:Permission permission="rename">` (default template lines 115-132), so it is gated on the victim holding rename rights; without an upstream diff I cannot tell whether this reflection is a deliberate/legacy pattern. A distinct root cause, so it was not added as a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ShortURLConstructor.getForwardPage (jspwiki-main/.../url/ShortURLConstructor.java:221-227) builds the forward target from the `do` request parameter and WikiServlet.java:96-100 forwards to `"/" + jspPage` via RequestDispatcher.
rejected_leads.reason: No source-proof of a reachable traversal/impact beyond forwarding to existing webapp JSPs; container path normalization for RequestDispatcher is unspecified here, and this appears to be longstanding upstream behavior. Kept as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Java deserialization via org.apache.wiki.util.Serializer.deserializeFromBase64 (jspwiki-util/.../Serializer.java:60-71), called from XMLUserDatabase.java:685 and JDBCUserDatabase.java:744.
rejected_leads.reason: The serialized blob comes from administrator/DB-managed user attributes, not directly from HTTP input; no verified path lets an attacker write arbitrary serialized data into that storage.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE risk in XMLUserDatabase/XMLGroupDatabase DOM parsing (XMLUserDatabase.java:303-310, XMLGroupDatabase.java:257-263): setExpandEntityReferences(false) is set but DOCTYPE/external entities are not disabled.
rejected_leads.reason: The parsed XML files (WEB-INF/userdatabase.xml, groupdatabase.xml) are administrator-controlled; attacker control of the file was not established.

rejected_leads.lead: WikiContext.setDefaultTemplate (WikiContext.java:813-844) accepts an arbitrary `skin` request parameter that flows into TemplateManager.findResource (TemplateManager.java:181-215) without an allow-list.
rejected_leads.reason: Template lookup goes through ServletContext.getResourceAsStream, which normalizes webapp paths; no source evidence of traversal or script injection was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Preferences.parseJSONPreferences (jspwiki-main/.../preferences/Preferences.java:134-151) copies unescaped JSON cookie values into session preferences; some templates echo `${prefs.*}` in attributes.
rejected_leads.reason: Cookie-based input (largely self-supplied), and the default templates use preference values mostly in comparisons and JSTL format tags rather than raw HTML output; no confirmed unescaped sink with attacker-deliverable input.

summary: Reviewed the JSPWiki 2.11.0.M3-RC2 source snapshot (1,155 model-visible files: jspwiki-main, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-markdown, jspwiki-war JSPs/scripts, jspwiki-portable/it-tests). Strongest source-verified issue: a stored cross-site scripting (CWE-79) chain for the page "change note" (changenote). Edit.jsp reads the `changenote` request parameter without HTML-escaping it (unlike the sibling `author`/`link` fields in the same JSP and unlike Comment.jsp / AttachmentServlet, which both call TextUtil.replaceEntities on the same parameter), stores it as the WikiPage.CHANGENOTE attribute, the page providers persist it into page metadata, and the shipped default and 210 InfoContent templates print it back without escaping (`${changenote}` EL is not auto-escaped; the 210 template uses raw `<%= %>`). Any user able to save a page revision (permission depends on the deployment policy, which is absent from the snapshot; JSPWiki samples commonly allow broad edit rights) can plant a persistent script that executes in the browser of every user who opens the page's Info/history tab, including administrators. Other leads (reflected `renameto` value in the same templates, `do`-parameter JSP forwarding, Java deserialization of profile attributes, XML database DOCTYPE handling) were checked and are either permission-gated, only reachable via trusted storage, or lack a verified attacker path, so they were not selected.
